questions.prompt: Why is the version part of the write contract in the CRUD lab? Explain the lost-update scenario it prevents and how the client participates.

keyPoints.text: Two clients read the task at version 1, and A saves a title change first.
keyPoints.quote: Suppose two clients read task 7 at version 1. Client A changes the title and saves.

keyPoints.text: Without a condition, B's full replacement would erase A's change.
keyPoints.quote: An unconditional write would erase A's title change.

keyPoints.text: Each writer must send the version it read so the server can tell current from outdated edits.
keyPoints.quote: so the server can distinguish a current edit from an outdated one.

keyPoints.text: The version travels as a quoted numeric ETag.
keyPoints.quote: The API exposes the version as a quoted numeric ETag.

keyPoints.text: The client echoes it in If-Match on PUT or DELETE.
keyPoints.quote: A client sends that value in If-Match on PUT or DELETE.

questions.prompt: Describe the lab's narrow conditional-request protocol and the compare-and-change rule inside the store.

keyPoints.text: No precondition gives 428, bad tag syntax 400, an outdated but valid version 412.
keyPoints.quote: missing preconditions return 428, unsupported or malformed tag syntax returns 400, and a valid but outdated version returns 412.

keyPoints.text: Wildcards, weak tags and tag lists are deliberately not supported.
keyPoints.quote: Wildcards, weak tags and lists are intentionally unsupported here.

keyPoints.text: Releasing the lock between compare and assign lets two writers both pass.
keyPoints.quote: Reading a version, releasing the lock, and later taking another lock to assign the item still permits two writers to pass the comparison.

keyPoints.text: Replace holds one lock across find, compare, construct and store.
keyPoints.quote: TaskStore.Replace holds one lock while it finds the current item, compares expected and actual versions, constructs the replacement and stores it.

keyPoints.text: Only one of two writers carrying the same current version can advance the item.
keyPoints.quote: Exactly one of two writers carrying the same current version can advance that item in this process.

questions.prompt: How do title validation and the process-local lock relate to version checking, and what changes when the store becomes a real database?

keyPoints.text: Bad titles are rejected before any store mutation.
keyPoints.quote: A blank or oversized title is rejected before the store mutates anything.

keyPoints.text: A valid title and a current version are independent decisions.
keyPoints.quote: A valid title does not prove a version is current, and a current version does not make a blank title acceptable.

keyPoints.text: Trim happens before the length rule and before storage.
keyPoints.quote: Trimming occurs before the title length contract is evaluated and before storage.

keyPoints.text: Two app instances would have two locks and two dictionaries.
keyPoints.quote: Two application instances would have separate locks and separate dictionaries.

keyPoints.text: A durable version needs the database operation to express the expected version and a no-row outcome.
keyPoints.quote: Durable implementation requires the database operation itself to express the expected version, plus an outcome for no matching row.
